title: Finite graded free cover with an internal shifted grading
statement: Let k be a field, S=k[x_0,x_1] with its total-degree grading, and M a finitely generated internally integer-graded S-module with S_n M_j contained in M_(n+j). With the shift convention of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2), there exist a free S-module F in the ring universe, a finite basis b indexed by Fin r, an internal integer grading G compatible with homogeneous scalar multiplication, integer shifts d with b_a in G_(-d_a), and a degree-zero surjective S-linear map F to M. The universe of M can be different from that of k.

proof.text: Apply exists_finite_homogeneous_generators to obtain a finite homogeneous generating family and a surjective linear map.

Flatten polynomial coefficients into finitely supported coefficient functions, and define each shifted degree submodule by support in the fiber of total degree plus generator shift. The support decomposition is internal because fibers partition the coefficient index set; transport this decomposition along the coefficient linear equivalence.

Coefficientwise homogeneity shows multiplication by a homogeneous polynomial raises shifted degree, basis vectors have the prescribed shifts, and the generator map sends each graded source component into the corresponding target component. Surjectivity is inherited from the generator map.

theorem exists_graded_free_cover {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) M]
    [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) M]
    (ℳ : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) (hℳ : DirectSum.IsInternal ℳ)
    (hsmul : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (s : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x : M),
      s ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n → x ∈ ℳ j → s • x ∈ ℳ ((n : ℤ) + j)) :
    ∃ (F : ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k))
      (𝒢 : ℤ → AddSubgroup F) (r : ℕ) (d : Fin r → ℤ)
      (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) F)
      (q : F →ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k] M),
      DirectSum.IsInternal 𝒢 ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (s : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x : F),
        s ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n → x ∈ 𝒢 j → s • x ∈ 𝒢 ((n : ℤ) + j)) ∧
      (∀ a : Fin r, b a ∈ 𝒢 (-(d a))) ∧
      (∀ (j : ℤ) (x : F), x ∈ 𝒢 j → q x ∈ ℳ j) ∧ Function.Surjective q
